answer: The originality bar tightens adaptively: as more low-quality answers appear in an epoch, the bar for what counts as a coherent answer rises, so a coordinated fake campaign has to raise the quality of every single alias to stay under the radar. This is durable because the trusted grader set only grows through bootstrap capacity, preventing a sudden takeover by a large new flock. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation. Consider a cipher as the anchor of the cost.
